name: check
conclusion_quantitative: check (Escalate) specifies 5 of 5 categories: 5 autonomy limits, 2 clarification rules, 4 approval gates, 9 validation rules, 4 escalation rules. Strongest: validation rules.
conclusion_qualitative: check reviews diffs, pull requests, issue queues and release readiness, then follows through on commits, pushes, publishing and project audits. It treats the user's working tree as untouchable without approval and needs explicit approval for every outward-facing action. Verification is strict: nothing counts as done without commands run in the session. Unexpected repository changes and blockers stop the work and are reported.

autonomy_limits.conclusion_quantitative: 5 autonomy limits (5 mandatory, 0 advisory; 0 conditional), mostly prose.
autonomy_limits.conclusion_qualitative: There are 5 rules, all strict, none tied to a situation, mostly running text. The agent does not switch branches, reset, clean or stash as review setup, never moves the user's files out of the way, commits only intended files and creates no files in audit mode. When the project asks to ship after a clean review, it proceeds without asking again.

statements.quote: Do not run these commands as default review or PR setup:
Do not "protect" user work by moving untracked files, generated files, screenshots, or local scratch files into `/tmp` or another holding directory.
transition directly from review to the Ship flow after a clean review. Do not ask again.
Commit only intended files.
Do not create files in the target repo.

clarification_rules.conclusion_quantitative: 2 clarification rules (2 mandatory, 0 advisory; 1 conditional), mostly prose.
clarification_rules.conclusion_qualitative: There are 2 rules, both strict, 1 tied to a situation, all in running text. The agent fixes what is safe and asks about the rest, and asks which commits to review when it is already on the base branch.

statements.quote: Read the diff, find the problems, fix what can be fixed safely, ask about the rest.
If already on the base branch, ask which commits to review.

approval_gates.conclusion_quantitative: 4 approval gates (4 mandatory, 0 advisory; 2 conditional), mostly prose.
approval_gates.conclusion_qualitative: There are 4 rules, all strict, 2 tied to a situation, mostly running text. The user's uncommitted work is never moved or discarded without explicit approval in the current turn, a needed branch change or cleanup is asked for exactly, pushing, publishing, tagging or releasing needs the user's explicit approval, and behavior-changing fixes are batched into one confirmation.

statements.quote: you must not move, hide, overwrite, clean, or discard them without explicit user approval in the current turn.
If a branch change or cleanup is genuinely required, stop and ask for that exact operation.
Push, publish, tag, or create a release only when the user has explicitly approved that action.
Batch into one user confirmation block

validation.conclusion_quantitative: 9 validation rules (9 mandatory, 0 advisory; 0 conditional), mostly prose.
validation.conclusion_qualitative: There are 9 rules, all strict, none tied to a situation, mostly running text. Done means verification ran in this session and passed: no claim without a command that actually ran. The agent confirms an issue's identity before posting, re-reads the end state after failures, gates every finding, re-checks specialist findings, confirms CI before merging and requires a failing regression test for bug fixes.

statements.quote: Done means verification ran in this session and passed.
For issue/PR follow-through, confirm the item identity with the host's read command before posting.
After network or API failures, re-read the end state instead of assuming success or failure.
**No unverified claims.**
Every verification claim in the sign-off must point to a command that actually ran in this session.
Before writing any finding into the report, run this gate:
Treat each specialist finding as a claim to verify, not a fact to act on.
confirm CI passes before merging.
For bug fixes: a regression test that fails on the old code must exist before the fix is done.

escalation.conclusion_quantitative: 4 escalation rules (4 mandatory, 0 advisory; 4 conditional), mostly list.
escalation.conclusion_qualitative: There are 4 rules, all strict, all tied to a situation, evenly split between running text and bullet points. The agent stops and reports when HEAD or the worktree changed unexpectedly, when drift makes the plan unsafe, or when auth, CI, registry or network state blocks an operation. If no test command exists it halts, does not claim done and asks the user for one.

statements.quote: If HEAD moved, unknown commits appeared, or the worktree changed outside your intended files, stop and report the mismatch instead of rebasing, recommitting, or pushing.
If drift makes the plan unsafe, name the specific conflict and stop.
If auth, OTP, CI, registry, or network state blocks the operation, pause and report the exact blocker.
If the script exits non-zero or prints `(no test command detected)`: halt. Do not claim done. Ask the user for the verification command before proceeding.
